Source: MoU signed 25 June 2025 in Luanda (U.S.-Africa Business Summit) between the Government of Sierra Leone and CEC Africa (Sierra Leone) Limited (CECASL) to develop West Africa's first U.S.-sourced LNG import terminal; co-developed with AG&P and current fuel supplier BB Energy (BBE); Nant Power sponsors TCQ Power and Anergi Group partner in the terminal; backed by U.S. DFC. Terminal enables the 108 MW Nant Power Project (financial close Jan 2025, initially LPG-fired) to transition to LNG per its PPA. US Embassy Freetown announcement puts the investment at ~$150 million and the terminal in Freetown, to be constructed and supplied by AG&P.
ResearcherNotesProject: Location 'Freetown' held at approximate accuracy: the verifiable ref is African Energy's 2021 'ESIA tender for Freetown LNG terminal' piece (IFC + GasLog then developing the terminal, offtaker the 90MW Western Area Power Generation Project at Kissy Dock; article is bot-blocked live (HTTP 403) but content confirmed via Wayback snapshot 20250113035635). The 2025 CECASL/AG&P MoU pages verified here do not name the city; the US Embassy Freetown social post ('LNG terminal in Freetown', $150m) is not machine-verifiable. Same project lineage: TCQ Power was the WAPGP/Nant developer in both iterations; the 2021 IFC/GasLog development did not proceed (Nant closed financing on LPG in Jan 2025) and the 2025 MoU relaunches the terminal under CECASL/AG&P. Precise site (likely Kissy, Freetown, adjacent to the Nant plant) to be confirmed - see qa. Capacity not yet published. Floating-vs-onshore configuration not yet published.
